newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares edge higher, seen moving ahead.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares edge higher, seen moving ahead.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed on Monday and market participants expressed confidence that prices would continue to rise until the end of the year.
The 10-share SBI index rose 0.11 percent or 1.29 points to 1,192.8 -- the fifth consecutive day of the gains..
"Foreign investors are as active as they used to be (before the November 10 general election) and that should keep the upward trend in place until the end of the year," a trader said.
Turnover fell to 106.4 million tolars from 235.6 million. Overall seven shares rose, seven fell, three remained unchanged and eight were untraded.
Drug maker Lek's A issue, which has dominated trade since its debut in September, was the most active share, easing 0.94 percent to 20,010 tolars on volume of 2,288.
Traders said Lek's fell was a technical reaction to its recent strength.
Bank Vipa was the biggest gainer, firming 2.38 percent to 43,000 tolars on volume of 18 shares.

Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, falling 20.75 percent to 9,320 tolars on volume of 1,418 shares. Traders said Dadas was off following payment of its dividend. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
